decisions.reason: As a publicly emphasized flagship close to the confectionery core and reinforced by a gold medal, it carries strong reputational commitment and little pressure for withdrawal.

Management would still persist with this core bread variant because it fits established capabilities and has already been publicly launched, though overlap in the rye assortment keeps some pruning risk alive.

This bread remains close enough to the traditional range for commitment to continue, but its more niche profile and similarity to other rye products make it one of the easier candidates for later rationalization.

Even beside the stronger stollen flagship, the firm is likely to keep this seasonal variant because it sits squarely in its confectionery tradition and abandoning it would mean reversing a recent visible launch.
Having been presented as a newest 'Meisterstück', this ancient grain bread benefits from public commitment and a strong fit with artisanal baking, making management inclined to continue it.
